html:
The San Carlos Apache are a Western Apache people of southeastern Arizona, on the San Carlos and Gila rivers. The San Carlos Apache Indian Reservation was created in 1872.

The Western Apache (Ndee) lived by farming small plots, gathering mescal and acorns, hunting and raiding. In the 1870s the United States made San Carlos the centre of a policy of concentration, forcing Chiricahua, Yavapai and other bands onto the hot, crowded reservation. Soldiers called it "Hell's Forty Acres". Geronimo broke out from San Carlos several times in the Apache Wars.

In 1930 the Coolidge Dam flooded much of the river valley, including the old agency. The reservation today is one of the largest in the United States. Neighbours include the White Mountain Apache; see also Apache.
